tools.when: The dedicated Windows counterpart to REMnux: the disposable, snapshotted VM where you actually detonate and debug regained Windows samples.
tools.install: On a clean Windows 10/11 VM, download install.ps1 and run '.\install.ps1'

tools.name: SIFT Workstation
tools.desc: SANS' free incident-response/forensics Ubuntu distro (installed via the Cast installer) bundling timeline analysis, carving, registry/memory forensics — a forensics-first companion for triaging recovered disk images.
tools.when: Move from analyzing the sample to analyzing the machine it ran on: timeline a recovered image for persistence, lateral movement, and other hands-on artifacts.
tools.install: sudo cast install teamdfir/sift-saltstack (or download the SIFT VM)

domains.name: Purple Team, BAS & Adversary Emulation
domains.tagline: Validate your detections by emulating real adversaries, running atomic TTPs, and mapping coverage against MITRE ATT&CK.

tools.name: MITRE Caldera
tools.desc: Automated adversary emulation platform built on ATT&CK, now an Apache project: deploy agents, craft adversary profiles from ATT&CK techniques, and run them against your own estate for blue-team validation.
tools.when: Build a repeatable adversary operation once and re-run it after every detection change or control rollout.

tools.name: Adversary Emulation Library
tools.desc: MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense's library of full (APT29, FIN6, Turla) and micro (webshells, process injection) emulation plans in human-readable plus machine-readable YAML for Caldera.
tools.when: Execute a threat-intel-grounded scenario as a ready-made purple-team script instead of writing one from scratch.

tools.name: Atomic Red Team
tools.desc: MITRE-aligned library of small, portable detection tests; each atomic test documents a technique's exact procedure plus the logs and telemetry a defender should see if their detection works.
tools.when: Prove a specific detection fires by running the precise TTP procedure it was built to catch.

tools.name: AtomicTestHarnesses
tools.desc: Red Canary's PowerShell module (Python for macOS/Linux) that executes many variations of a single technique and validates the telemetry each variation generates.
tools.when: Check your detections hold up across technique variants, not just the single canonical procedure.

tools.name: Infection Monkey
tools.desc: Open-source BAS/adversary emulation platform (Guardicore/Akamai) whose agent self-propagates across a network via real exploiters and reports to the Monkey Island console.
tools.when: Automated lateral-movement and control-gap testing on a lab segment or isolated data-center island.

tools.name: SafeBreach Validate
tools.desc: Commercial BAS pioneer: lightweight simulators on endpoints, network, and cloud run 30,000+ attack methods from its Hacker's Playbook to continuously validate controls.
tools.when: Continuous, enterprise-scale security-control validation when you have budget for a licensed BAS product.

tools.name: Stratus Red Team
tools.desc: Cloud-oriented BAS: 'Atomic Red Team for the cloud', with granular AWS/Azure/GCP/Entra ID/K8s techniques that detonate then clean up after themselves; the star of the cloud-bas category.
tools.when: When your attack surface is cloud-first — jump to the cloud-bas category where Stratus is the pick.

tools.name: DeTT&CT
tools.desc: Rabobank's framework to administer and score data-source quality, visibility, and detection per ATT&CK technique, then export the resulting coverage as ATT&CK Navigator layers.
tools.when: Build a scored, evidence-based map of your detection and visibility coverage and prioritize blue-team effort on the gaps.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK (website)
tools.desc: The authoritative knowledge base: adversary tactics, techniques, sub-techniques, threat groups, and the data sources needed to detect them.
tools.when: Resolve technique IDs and read detection guidance before any scoring, emulation, or rule building.

tools.name: ATT&CK Navigator
tools.desc: Web app for annotating and exploring ATT&CK matrices via shareable layer files; load DeTT&CT or VECTR output to render coverage heatmaps.
tools.when: Visualize and communicate detection coverage across the matrix during and after purple exercises.

tools.name: Stratus Red Team
tools.desc: Datadog's cloud BAS: a self-contained Go binary that detonates granular cloud attack techniques for AWS, Azure, GCP, Entra ID, and K8s, mapped to the ATT&CK cloud matrix, with automatic warmup and cleanup.
tools.when: Validate your cloud SIEM detections against real TTPs on a dedicated sandbox cloud account, never production.

tools.name: CloudGoat 2
tools.desc: Rhino Security Labs' 'Vulnerable by Design' AWS/Azure deployment tool that builds intentionally vulnerable, CTF-style scenarios for practicing cloud attack paths.
tools.when: Stand up an authorized practice range in a throwaway cloud account to rehearse TTPs before running real emulation.

tools.name: VECTR
tools.desc: Free purple-team platform (Security Risk Advisors) that tracks red/blue test cases, campaigns, and per-tool detection/prevention outcomes measured against MITRE ATT&CK over time.
tools.when: Record exercise results and trend detection coverage over months so purple-team improvements are measurable.

domains.name: Threat Intelligence, Sharing & Detection Engineering
domains.tagline: Enrich your own defenses: share and consume intel, pivot on IOCs, and write portable detections against common frameworks.

tools.name: MISP
tools.desc: The open-source intelligence sharing platform: community-synced events, TLP/orgs, feed syncing, and a REST API for exchanging malware and attack indicators with trusted partners at scale.
tools.when: Run or sync a MISP instance when you need structured, governed intel sharing across your team, an ISAC-style community, or your own feed ingestion pipeline.
tools.install: sudo bash INSTALL/INSTALL.sh from MISP codebase (Ubuntu/Kali): wget -O /tmp/INSTALL.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MISP/MISP/2.4/INSTALL/INSTALL.sh && sudo bash /tmp/INSTALL.sh

tools.name: OpenCTI
tools.desc: Filigran's open cyber-threat-intelligence platform: ingests from 100+ connectors into a STIX-based knowledge graph with worker-managed import, investigations, and STIX/TAXII 2 exchange.
tools.when: Stand up a central intel drive when you want automated feed ingestion (MISP, MITRE, abuse.ch) correlated into entities, reports, and indicators rather than raw IOC lists.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/OpenCTI-Platform/docker.git && cp .env.sample .env && docker compose up -d

tools.name: TAXII 2
tools.desc: The STIX/TAXII 2.x protocol (OASIS standard) feed providers and ISACs use to push/pull structured intelligence; consume collections or publish your own vetted IOCs to partners.
tools.when: Connect your SIEM/intel stack to TAXII feed endpoints, or publish your own vetted indicators to partners without building custom transport.
tools.install: preinstalled (protocol); pip install stix2 for client ingestion

tools.name: Sigma
tools.desc: The generic, SIEM-agnostic detection format: YAML rules for log semantics; sigma-cli compiles them to Splunk, Elastic, Loki, QRadar, Sentinel, and dozens of other query languages.
tools.when: Author detection once and ship it anywhere: port a SigmaHQ rule, run sigma convert --target <siem>, and validate the query against logs before tuning.
tools.install: pipx install sigma-cli && git clone https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma

tools.name: Atomic Red Team
tools.desc: Red Canary's adversary-simulation library mapping 700+ ATT&CK techniques to executable test definitions, used to prove a detection fires — or stays silent.
tools.when: Verify Sigma or SIEM rules against real technique behavior: run the matching atom, watch your alert pipeline, and tune the rule before deployment.

tools.name: YARA
tools.desc: Binary pattern-matching rule engine for malware families and byte-level IOCs; complements SIEM rules when the evidence is a file, not a log (fuller coverage in the malware domain).
tools.when: Match dropped samples or artifacts against signature rules, or encode a family signature your feed team can't express in a log query.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK
tools.desc: The common knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, and data sources that Sigma rules, atoms, defenders, and coverage reports all annotate against — a reference framework, not a tool.
tools.when: Map and measure detection coverage: tag rules with technique IDs, standardize on its vocabulary for alerts and reports, or browse technique details before writing a rule.

tools.name: AlienVault OTX
tools.desc: Free open threat exchange (AT&T/LevelBlue): subscribe to community pulses, query indicator enrichment, and sync IOCs via the OTXv2 SDK or DirectConnect agents.
tools.when: Commercial-grade feeds with zero setup: register, grab an API key, and enrich or ingest IOCs within the hour — the broadest free pulse ecosystem.

tools.name: ThreatFox
tools.desc: abuse.ch's malware-IOC feed: submit and query malpedia-labeled IOCs (IPs, domains, URLs, hashes), with CSV/JSON dumps, Suricata ruleset, and MISP event exports.
tools.when: Pull current malware IOCs into your SIEM or blocklist, or pivot a domain/IP to its associated malware family (also covered in ioc-pivoting).

tools.name: MalwareBazaar
tools.desc: abuse.ch's sample-sharing database: search by hash, signature, or imphash, download malware samples, and pull hourly/daily batch feeds.
tools.when: Grab reference samples or up-to-date hashes by tag or signature for your sandbox, YARA hunting, or detection validation.

tools.name: URLhaus
tools.desc: abuse.ch's malicious-URL feed complementing ThreatFox: a plain-text URL list plus RPZ, hostfile, and Suricata/Snort rulesets for proxy and log matching.
tools.when: Blocklist or hunt URLs in proxy/DNS logs; the plain-text URL list catches malware download paths with low false positives.

tools.name: IntelOwl
tools.desc: Self-hosted aggregation and analysis platform: one request runs a file/IP/domain/hash through 100+ analyzers (OTX, ThreatFox, MalwareBazaar, VirusTotal, GreyNoise, YARA) and chains them with pivots.
tools.when: Pivot every incoming IOC across your whole free-vendor stack automatically, or plug it into SOAR/MISP/OpenCTI for repeatable, centralized enrichment.

tools.name: MISP
tools.desc: (Also in threat-sharing): its correlation engine links identical and high-fidelity-cluster attributes across every event in your instance and its federated communities, surfacing related infrastructure from others' incidents.
tools.when: Correlate a suspicious attribute against your event history to find linked campaigns, reused C2, or related infrastructure while investigating an alert.

tools.name: ThreatFox
tools.desc: (Also in analytics-marketplaces): excels at pivoting a file hash to the hosts and IPs that served it plus its family label — the fastest 'what is this IOC attached to' lookup.
tools.when: Instant pivoting with zero infrastructure: paste a hash, domain, or IP and get malware family, threat type, and related IOCs from the community dataset.

tools.name: Pulsedive
tools.desc: Free IOC portal combining passive/active scans, risk scores, ATT&CK tags, and a pivot/Explore query language across its indicator database, with a browser extension for on-page enrichment.
tools.when: Enrich an indicator with risk scores and relationship pivots without standing up a platform: free account, pivot graphs, and exports for quick triage.
